new_real_linux_checks: An actual competing process cannot acquire the round journal lock while native work is in flight; SIGKILL releases the lock and a new process resumes from disk without another native dispatch.
SIGKILL after a simulated provider deletion but before its acknowledgement preserves the independent delete intent; restart performs exact readback without sending the same deletion again.
SIGTERM during the bound native wait stops work and completes the unified cleanup, with the controller deleted last and acceptance remaining failed after a stop request.
Partial initialization with only source A cleans exactly the resources that exist, without inventing source B or a native grant.
An unprivileged Linux process encountering a non-writable journal directory is refused before initialization interfaces execute. Durable journal files retain private permissions.
existing_regressions: Staged initialization, original request binding, partial and unknown outcomes, restart, stop and exact resource reconciliation
Existing Linode adapter request construction, once-only creation, definite rejection versus unknown outcome, encrypted request retention and identity-checked cleanup
Source A/B registration, native A1 cleanup confirmation, cooldown, A2 retry and B isolation with simulated provider and DNS responses
Fixed PHP CLI grant validation, queue isolation, private runtime loading, exact task cleanup and permission restoration
Unarmed package hashes, LF normalization, local staging, durable journals and cleanup evidence readback

first_run.reason: The temporary launcher required zero skipped tests but included three Windows-only sharing tests. Eight fixed-entry tests and 150 Python tests passed; there were no test failures or errors. The zero-skip summary assertion stopped the run before PHP service tests.
first_run.correction: Select test_driver_journal.JournalTests for Linux rather than the entire module. The Windows-only class is excluded; Linux tests still must report zero skipped cases.
